analysis.title: Memory Market Update: Perplexing top-down vs bottom-up view; Thoughts into 3Q earnings; NT earnings conviction to calm fears
key_insights: Global top-three memory shares (Samsung Electronics, SK hynix, Micron) are down 42% on average from their recent peaks. JPM attributes the drop to softer Frontier AI lab revenue run-rate trends, a wider Neo-Cloud CDS spread, tighter risk appetite and doubts about AI capex sustainability.

JPM calls this the third interim correction since the AI trade began, after July 2024 (Yen-carry unwind) and mid-2025 (HBM ASP correction speculation). It reads the current price action as pricing a down-cycle as early as 2027, with Q/Q memory prices turning negative.
JPM sees limited signs of a crack in bottom-up fundamentals: spot prices trending up, HBM ASP negotiations biased to the upside, and long-term agreement (LTA) order visibility extended.
The biggest disconnects JPM names are (1) AI capex slowing to under $1.5T in 2027 on funding risks, per the US hardware team, and (2) what catalysts could reverse the sentiment.
Memory stocks have historically fallen 49% peak-to-trough over the past four downcycles (GFC -71%, pre-AI -53%) and bottomed at 0.9-1.2x trailing P/B.

Past downcycles shared three signals: spot/contract prices plateauing then correcting sharply, unexpected inventory build at memory makers and OEMs, and demand slowdown signals from other tech supply chains.

Current status on those signals: 8Gb DDR4/5 spot prices are flat to +4% month to date, inventory is extremely tight with pricing talks centered on 2028/2029, and there are limited order cuts in the AI complex alongside continued price hikes.
CXMT's 4F² development stoked another round of fear. JPM believes past downcycles came from demand more than supply expansion and expects CXMT to be less of a threat.

Into 3Q earnings, JPM says the memory trade is a battleground between momentum investors (following EPS revisions and y/y pricing) and value investors betting on a higher-for-longer cycle. Near-term earnings color is the primary driver of share prices.

DRAM ASP growth was +54% / +27% / +236% y/y in 2024 / 2025 / 2026E. Sentiment on 2027E pricing is cautious because CSP AI capex is sustainability-linked to widening negative FCF and a rate-hike environment.
JPM thinks agentic CPU-related memory demand is the most under-appreciated source of demand upside.

Company watch items: SK hynix HBM4 execution and yield rumors; Samsung HBM business targets and HBM4 pricing negotiations; Kioxia 4Q26 NAND blended pricing and QLC demand. Vendors' ability to offset B2C softness with B2B strength and 2027E bit supply growth commentary are also in focus.
The HBM4E de-spec in Rubin Ultra and the gap between larger AI context windows and slower HBM content upgrades raised doubts over the inelasticity of AI memory demand in the past 3 months.
Four pillars JPM sees resetting sentiment: HBM content re-acceleration, supply discipline, broader AI demand drivers, and shareholder returns (most important near term).

Korean and Japanese large-cap memory stocks have retraced to pre-buyback-announcement levels and trade around 3x forward P/E. A credible buyback and dividend framework could shift the debate to how much downside is already priced in.

JPM's DCF shows Samsung at 2-3x P/E (27/28E) and 0.9x-1.5x P/B, and SK hynix at 2.0-2.8x P/E and 1.0-1.5x P/B, which JPM says prices in a downcycle that has not materialized. Memory shares typically react 6-9 months ahead, implying an earnings peak as early as 1H27E.
Past downcycle share drawdowns: -50% in 14/16, -43% in 18/19, -47% in 21/23, and -71% in the GFC. The current -42% is already close to those.
Short-term preference is SK hynix (OW) over Samsung (OW) on a better shareholder return policy and higher TSR yield. JPM also likes Kioxia (OW) and Nanya Technology (OW).

Samsung DCF fair value per share ranges from W810,000 (bull) to W260,000 (extreme bear) against a W218,000 share price, implying +272% to +19%. SK hynix ranges from W3.9M to W1.47M against W1,277,000, implying +205% to +15%.

market_movers.rationale: SK hynix (000660.KS) is preferred over Samsung on superior shareholder return policy and higher TSR yield. It trades at about 2-3x 2027/28E P/E. The price target is the 5-Aug-26 level.
Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) trades at 2-3x 2027/28E P/E and 0.9-1.5x P/B, which JPM says prices in a downcycle without evidence. The price target is the 30-Jul-26 level.
Nanya Technology (2408.TW) is liked in Asia. The price target is the 9-Aug-26 level, after an upgrade to OW on 3-Jul-26.
Kioxia (285A.T) is liked in Asia. Its watch item is 4Q26 NAND blended pricing and the QLC NAND demand update.

sector_views.rationale: JPM sees limited evidence of a downcycle and signs of a stronger, longer upcycle over the last 1-3 months. Share prices already price in a historical-size drawdown.

earnings_insights: JPM previews 3Q26 earnings for memory makers: near-term earnings color outweighs long-term cycle evidence. Estimates are JPM's own, not consensus.
DRAM ASP y/y growth: +54% in 2024, +27% in 2025, +236% in 2026E (JPM estimate).
Samsung DCF base case 2027E revenue is W907,321bn (+30% y/y) and 2028E is W1,098,839bn (+21% y/y). 2026 revenue is W695,364bn (+108% y/y). These are JPM estimates.
SK hynix DCF base case 2027E revenue is W511,166bn (+51% y/y) and 2028E is W666,675bn (+30% y/y). 2026 revenue is W338,830bn (+249% y/y). These are JPM estimates.
Samsung 2027E EBIT is W522,618bn (57.6% margin) and 2028E is W664,508bn (60.5%). SK hynix 2027E EBIT is W395,125bn (77.3% margin) and 2028E is W507,846bn (76.2%). These are JPM estimates.
Samsung DRAM operating margin is 78% in 2026 and 2027E, falling to 71% by 2030E in the base case. In the extreme bear case it falls to 24%.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Exceptionally strong pricing growth after +54% (2024) and +27% (2025). Investors are watching for signs the upcycle is cooling.
Spot prices are not plateauing, which is a key early downcycle signal, so it does not support a down-cycle call.
A slowdown from funding risks is the key top-down risk to the memory demand outlook, per JPM's US hardware team.

trade_ideas.rationale: SK hynix has a superior shareholder return policy and higher TSR yield, and share prices already price a downcycle that has not materialized.

tension_points.bull_case: Spot prices are flat to up 4% month to date, inventory is extremely tight, order visibility extends to 2028/2029, HBM ASP negotiations lean upward, and agentic CPU memory demand adds upside. Samsung and SK hynix trade at 2-3x 2027/28E P/E.
tension_points.bear_case: AI capex could slow to under $1.5T in 2027 on funding risks. CSP free cash flow is widening negative in a rate-hike environment, and the HBM4E de-spec in Rubin Ultra raises doubts about demand inelasticity.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Spot and contract prices plateauing followed by a sharp correction, unexpected inventory building at memory makers and OEMs, or demand slowdown signals from other tech supply chains.

theme_stances.key_argument: Share prices presume a memory downcycle as early as 2027 that bottom-up fundamentals do not show.
theme_stances.evidence: we see limited signs of a crack from a bottom-up memory supply/demand fundamental angle
